comprehensiveness.criterion: Coverage of the two core approaches and their main variants
Coverage of decision contexts for when formal verification should be preferred
Coverage of decision contexts for when fuzzing should be preferred
Coverage of the core tradeoff dimensions: cost, coverage, and scalability
Coverage of both security and correctness assurance perspectives
Coverage of empirical evidence and real-world case material
Coverage of domain and system-type diversity within critical software
Coverage of hybrid, complementary, and workflow-integration perspectives
Coverage of limitations, prerequisites, and failure modes of each approach

insight.criterion: Principled comparative reasoning between formal verification and fuzzing
Rigor in handling assumptions, guarantees, and failure modes
Quality of tradeoff analysis on cost, coverage, and scalability
Context-sensitive decision framework for critical systems
Synthesis of complementary and hybrid strategies
Strength, originality, and practical value of conclusions

instruction_following.criterion: Directly answers the stated research question
Covers all mandated comparison dimensions and context
Includes explicit critical analysis beyond summary
Follows the required report format and markdown structure
Includes a 'Sources' section at the end with consulted materials

readability.criterion: Clarity and precision of language: Explains formal verification, fuzzing, and related concepts in clear, unambiguous prose with minimal unnecessary jargon; technical terms are defined when first introduced.

Logical organization and flow: Uses a coherent structure with effective sectioning, headings, and transitions so readers can easily follow the argument from background to tradeoffs, comparisons, and conclusions.

Accessibility of technical explanation: Makes complex methods, assumptions, and tradeoffs understandable to an informed research audience through concise explanations, examples, and well-integrated comparisons.

Effective presentation of evidence and visuals: Tables, figures, lists, and citations are readable, well-labeled, and directly support comprehension of cost, coverage, scalability, and security/correctness tradeoffs.

Style, concision, and formatting quality: Maintains a professional academic tone, avoids redundancy, uses consistent terminology and markdown formatting, and presents text in a polished, easy-to-scan manner.
